wheel_core.name: Hub core disc and rim
wheel_core.goal: Read 1) this is the player's tower centre, 2) whose class it is (Breaker). Under 0.3 s, by position alone; it must never compete with the slices or threat marks.
wheel_core.look: A quiet dark lens: near-black CRT glass with a single cyan rim at medium weight, a faint inner bevel and no fill gradient. It is the still eye of the board, one value step darker than the slices.
wheel_core.problems: Rim is the same weight and cyan as the code-base frame ring 100 px out, so the two rings blur into one cyan system; disc fill is flat with no material; at 320 px squint the hub vanishes into the gutters; the gap between hub rim and slice tips is uneven (slice wedges touch on some sides, 3 px gap on others).

wheel_core.name: Hub inner concentric rings (lens material)
wheel_core.goal: Give the hub lens a glass material so it reads as an object, not a hole; carries no information.
wheel_core.look: Either one deliberate inner bevel ring (hairline, one value step above the fill, light from the top-left per 3.6) or nothing; never a ring stack that reads as a target or a dial.
wheel_core.problems: draw_hub paints faint white rings at alpha 10 every 9 px from r 16 to r 36: invisible at 1080p and at 320 px, so the hub still reads flat; if raised as-is, five concentric rings would read as a bullseye under the BREAKER word and the emblem.

wheel_core.name: Hub class word (BREAKER)
wheel_core.goal: Confirm class identity once; secondary to the CELL-9 nameplate that says the same thing. Readable but never the first thing seen.
wheel_core.look: Anton in white with an ink keyline, sized to sit inside the lens with clear margin; or demoted to a class emblem only, with the word moved to the nameplate.
wheel_core.problems: Word duplicates the nameplate (CELL-9 // BREAKER); Anton at ~22 px with no keyline and pixel-stepped edges; text is centred low and crowds the lower rim; the nowords plate leaves an empty hub, which shows the label is carrying the identity instead of an emblem.

wheel_core.name: Hub class emblem (Breaker pick tick)
wheel_core.goal: Carry class identity without words; read as an emblem, not as a needle or pointer.
wheel_core.look: A proper Breaker class emblem from the class glyph set, centred, in the class accent at reduced value, inset like an engraving.
wheel_core.problems: Reads as a stray cyan pointer at 1 o'clock, which suggests a dial needle and conflicts with the real needle at sector 0; it is aliased (stair-stepped) and sits off-centre above the word; thin stroke below the 16 px glyph rule.

wheel_core.name: Slice tile frame (wedge outline)
wheel_core.goal: Separate the six tower slices and tell their TYPE by colour plus icon (bible 2.3: green repair, pink attack, cyan shield). Read the 6-way division in under 0.2 s.
wheel_core.look: Family-C CRT screen wedge: rounded inner and outer corners, a thin type-colour edge at fine weight with an ink line outside it, consistent inset from neighbours.
wheel_core.problems: Edge colours are hard to tell apart (shield teal, turret magenta, burst pink, repair lime-green all at the same thin weight); outline weight varies by slice as the texture bleeds into it; corner radii are uneven between the hub side and the rim side; the frame line is thinner than the HP bar inside it, so the bars read as the frame.

wheel_core.name: Slice programme screen texture
wheel_core.goal: Give each slice material and life (CRT programme screen) without carrying any information. Must stay a backdrop to the icon.
wheel_core.look: Low-contrast CRT texture in the type colour, scanlines and soft code text, value capped below the icon and below the red threat marks; one consistent treatment across all six.
wheel_core.problems: BURST slices carry a loud rainbow chromatic halo, the most saturated thing in the wheel, competing with red threat and reading as a non-existent status effect; texture contrast varies wildly between slice types (bright green waterfall on REPAIR, dark pink hex on TURRET, flat teal grid on SHIELD). Readable code text is a separate element (slice_screen_code_text).

wheel_core.name: Readable code and hex text in slice screens
wheel_core.goal: None; texture only. The slice screen may suggest code, but no legible word or digit may appear on the board (no-words / tallies-only rule).
wheel_core.look: Glyph noise below legibility: sub-8 px pseudo-characters or blurred columns under 10 percent contrast, the same density in all six slices; nothing that survives as a word in p1_nowords.
wheel_core.problems: Legible strings in the REPAIR waterfall ('goto fail', 'return 0', 'head') and hex columns in the TURRET screen survive in p1_nowords; they are the only words left on the nowords board and they sit right under the slice icons, adding texture contrast exactly where the icon needs a quiet ground.

wheel_core.name: Slice gutters and spokes
wheel_core.goal: Show the sector boundaries that line up with ring sectors outward (one radial strip per sector).
wheel_core.look: Even ink-black gutters, the same width as the ring gutters, so the 6 radial strips read continuously from hub to bezel.
wheel_core.problems: Slice gutters are visibly narrower than the ring gutters, so the radial strip breaks at the HP ring; gutter ends meet the hub at different depths; the sector line does not continue through the HP ring or the code-base frame.

wheel_core.name: BURST slice icon
wheel_core.goal: Read 'two-shot gun' (BURST) at a glance; identical silhouette on both BURST slices.
wheel_core.look: Bible 3.5 glyph: white silhouette, ink keyline at 7.5 percent, about 44 px, centred on the slice's visual centre, no glow.
wheel_core.problems: Starburst with a hole reads as 'explosion / damage taken' more than 'burst fire'; sits on the rainbow halo so its edge loses contrast; slightly off the wedge centroid (pushed toward the hub).

wheel_core.name: SHIELD slice icon
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice blocks 2' at a glance (PL10 ask 4).
wheel_core.look: Half-filled heater shield in white with ink keyline, same size and baseline rule as the other slice icons.
wheel_core.problems: Half-black fill reads as 'half broken' when the slice is intact; same shield shape as the gold warded mark and the cream Brace glyph, so three different meanings share one silhouette; when the slice breaks the red X lands on top of the icon and hides it.

wheel_core.name: TURRET slice icon (sword)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'single-shot gun' (TURRET).
wheel_core.look: A gun/turret glyph from the set that reads as ranged fire, same size and weight as the other icons.
wheel_core.problems: A sword reads as melee attack, not a turret shot; it is visibly thinner and smaller than the other icons and tilted, so it looks weaker; the red X is drawn over it.

wheel_core.name: REPAIR slice icon (bandage)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'mends 1 slice pip per turn'.
wheel_core.look: Crossed bandage glyph in white with keyline; consistent size and centring.
wheel_core.problems: Bandage detail (pad square) fills in at 320 px; the bright green code-waterfall texture under it fights the icon; slightly larger than the burst icon.

wheel_core.name: Slice HP bar set (2 capsules per slice, five pip states)
wheel_core.goal: Read intact / cracked / broken and which pips change THIS turn, under 0.5 s per slice. The bar owns geometry and the five pip states as one designed set: lit, lost to harm, lost to soak, mend pending, gone.
wheel_core.look: Thin floating capsules at the outer edge, equal length and gaps on all six slices, one end cap shape, ink under each; the five states differ by shape first (solid / slashed / soak-marked / outlined-plus / empty socket) and colour second.
wheel_core.problems: Capsules (r 132), threat trim (r 142) and HP ring (r 147-157) make three parallel green/red/salmon arcs within 25 px that merge; capsule ends inconsistent; bar length differs per slice; the code draws five pip states but they were never designed together, so one bar can show salmon and orange lost pips side by side (SHIELD sector 1, p2). State-specific problems sit in slice_pip_lost_harm, slice_pip_lost_soak, slice_pip_mend and slice_pip_gone.

wheel_core.name: Slice pip lost to harm this turn (salmon + slash)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this pip is lost at END TURN to enemy hits' on a slice, in the same family as the HP ring's and YOU tally's lost marks.
wheel_core.look: HARM red capsule with a clear white slash (Fine tier, ink under), or a hollowed capsule with a red slash; the same lost grammar as hp_ring and you_hp_tally.
wheel_core.problems: Salmon #FF968C with a 2 px white slash: the slash vanishes at 320 px and salmon sits next to the red threat trim at r 142, so the lost pip reads as part of the trim; it does not match the hp_ring lost red, so slice loss and player HP loss look like two different things.

wheel_core.name: Slice pip lost to SOAK (orange capsule, p2)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice pip pays for overflow instead of your HP' (the player's choice), distinct from a pip lost to harm in the same bar.
wheel_core.look: The new soak token (hue and shape clear of schedule orange, open call 1) applied to the capsule: for example a capsule with the soak mark notched in, never just a recoloured lost pip.
wheel_core.problems: tower_slice_bars' by_soak branch paints the pip SOAK_C #FF9628, nearly schedule orange; with no slash it reads as a lit pip in the wrong colour or as part of the orange soak rim arc beside it; next to the salmon harm pip in the same bar the two lost states differ only by a small hue step.

wheel_core.name: Slice pip mend pending (REPAIR heal preview) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this pip comes back at END TURN' (REPAIR mends 1). The only GAIN-preview mark on the tower.
wheel_core.look: GAIN-family capsule as an outline or ghost with a small plus, clearly a preview (not yet lit), in the same set as the lost states.
wheel_core.problems: Not in this state (no slice regains a pip in f1/f2); code draws a pale green (170,240,170) capsule with a white 3/3 dash, nearly identical to a lit green pip at 320 px, and the white dash is the same mark as the harm slash, so mend and loss would share a shape.

wheel_core.name: Slice pip already gone (empty socket) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read a pip lost in an earlier turn: socket empty, not a change this turn.
wheel_core.look: Dark empty socket with a hairline outline, quieter than any this-turn state, same geometry as a lit capsule.
wheel_core.problems: Not in this state (all slices at 2/2 before END TURN); code draws a dashed socket line that looks like the +2 dashed lane language and like the hp_ring gone segment only by chance.

wheel_core.name: Slice breaks-this-turn X
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice breaks at END TURN, its ability is lost' (sectors 1 and 2). Must be the strongest slice state.
wheel_core.look: A heavy ink-keylined X in harm red placed off the icon (corner), plus a state treatment of the whole wedge (hatch or dim preview) per bible 3.22 BROKEN; red X never sits over the icon.
wheel_core.problems: X is drawn over the icon and hides what will be lost; it is the same red and size as the gun-tracer impacts and the threat trim so it does not read as a state; no hatch/dim preview as the bible's BROKEN rule asks; the soaked variant (p2) turns the X orange, which collides with the schedule orange.

wheel_core.name: Threat trim on slices (now / next / later)
wheel_core.goal: Read which slices get hit THIS turn (solid red), next turn (dashed pale blue) and in two turns (dashed white). The first thing the eye finds on the wheel.
wheel_core.look: An LED arc on each slice's outer edge: solid harm red bold for now, dashed pale blue medium for next, dashed white fine for later; the only glowing element on the wheel.
wheel_core.problems: The three trims sit at r 142 / 146 / 150, so the next-turn and later trims are drawn ON the HP ring (r 147-157) and merge with it and the slice bars into a five-line band; next-turn pale blue matches the +1 lane colour (good) but at 3 px dashed over green HP it disappears; trim length (50 deg) differs from the slice bar span (about 42 deg) so the ends misalign.

wheel_core.name: Player HP ring (rim ring segments)
wheel_core.goal: Read the player's 15 HP around the tower and how many are lost this END TURN (6 red). Must agree with the YOU tally in the HUD.
wheel_core.look: 15 equal segments in a socket ring: green lit, harm red with a fine white slash for lost-this-turn, dark for gone; segment gaps aligned so groups of 5 are visible.
wheel_core.problems: No groups of 5 (the HUD tally uses groups, the ring does not), so the two HP displays do not match; the lost run always sits at the end of the ring (216-360 deg, over sectors 4-5) whatever slices are hit, so position on the ring suggests a sector meaning it does not have; red lost segments sit beside red threat trim and read as more threat; the ring is 10 px thick, thicker than the slice bars, so it reads as the wheel frame.

wheel_core.name: Code-base frame rings (cyan)
wheel_core.goal: Close the tower as one object and mark it as 'ours' (cyan, per 3.22).
wheel_core.look: One fine cyan ring at the HP ring's outer edge, with an ink line; not two.
wheel_core.problems: Two cyan rings drawn about 1 px apart (a doubled, uneven line) plus the hub rim give a cyan circle system with no job beyond 'ours'; the ring is crossed by the threat trims and the gun nubs; adds line noise without information.

wheel_core.name: Nudge ghost arrows (cyan triangles at sector 0)
wheel_core.goal: Hint that the tower can be turned (Spin cards). Tertiary.
wheel_core.look: Either remove (bible 3.22: draw no nudge buttons on the ring wheel until build settles it) or a pair of hollow cyan chevrons engraved in the bezel at the needle.
wheel_core.problems: Contradicts the bible 'Open' note (no nudge on the ring wheel); the hollow triangles sit on top of the ring-0 Worm cell and the gun nubs, cluttering the most loaded spot on the board; they look like play/rewind media buttons.

wheel_core.name: Gun tracer line (default fire)
wheel_core.goal: Read each gun's default target as a line from slice rim to target; after threat, before HUD. The line only: each result end mark is its own element (gun_result_*).
wheel_core.look: Cyan dashed tracer with ink edge, one dash rhythm shared with nothing else on the board (or matched deliberately to lane dashes), ending on the target cell centre or token, never on an edge.
wheel_core.problems: Turret tracer to the Adjuster crosses its gold edge, so the hit point is ambiguous; dash 10/4 differs from lane dashes 10/7 by a near miss; two-shot BURST shown only as two lines 9 px apart; a second, thinner tracer style exists in p3 (resolve_fire_lines) and an idle stub style (gun_idle_stub).

wheel_core.name: Gun result: hit (white impact dot)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'the shot lands and deals damage' at the tracer end.
wheel_core.look: A white spark / impact glyph with ink, at least token-detail size (16 px+), in one set with the armor, ward and shield-pop results.
wheel_core.problems: A 14 px white dot, too small to read as a hit and the same shape as turn dots and wave-arc width dots; at the Adjuster it sits on the gold edge.

wheel_core.name: Gun result: armor bounce (steel ricochet) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read 'the shot does nothing: armored' (Payload, Adjuster in strike phase).
wheel_core.look: Steel ricochet glyph with ink (STEEL token), same size and family as the hit spark; ties to armor_cap.
wheel_core.problems: Not reached in f1/f2 (no gun targets the Payload); code draws a small steel mark that has never been judged at size or next to the armor cap.

wheel_core.name: Gun result: ward bounce (gold ricochet) - LATENT on the plates, reached by the sim
wheel_core.goal: Read 'the shot is weakened by the Adjuster's ward' (h 0 here).
wheel_core.look: Ricochet glyph in BOSS_GOLD with ink, keyed to warded_mark and ward_arc; same set as hit and armor.
wheel_core.problems: The sim reaches it in f2 (BURST sector 4's two shots into warded Packet uid 6, both 'ward', h 0) but p2/p3 draw no tracers, so the glyph has never been seen; it must be designed with gun_tracers_preview.

wheel_core.name: Gun result: shield pop (cyan) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read 'the shot strips a shield layer, not HP' (Jammer).
wheel_core.look: Cyan pop glyph that matches shield_bracket, same set as the other results.
wheel_core.problems: No shielded Jammer in this state; cyan pop would share NET_CYAN with the tracer itself, so it needs a shape that does not vanish into the line.

wheel_core.name: Gun result: sealed (stale branch) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: None: the seal mechanic was removed in E9. Decision element: delete the branch or design it.
wheel_core.look: Recommendation: retire (no look); if a seal returns, it gets a glyph from the results set.
wheel_core.problems: gun_tracers10 still has a live 'sealed' branch (dark disc, white 2.4 px ring at ri + 16) that would draw a mark meaning nothing in the current rules.

wheel_core.name: Idle-gun tracer stub - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this gun has no target this turn' without a word (pairs with no_target_tag, and is the nowords form of it).
wheel_core.look: A short cyan stub ending in an empty-target mark (open ring or bar), same tracer family, clearly not a shot.
wheel_core.problems: Code draws a 2 px cyan dash 4/8 line from r 145 to 175: thinner than every tracer, crosses the trim and HP ring band, and ends in nothing, so it reads as a stray dash; it stays in nowords where the NO TARGET tag is gone.

wheel_core.name: Gun tracers under the plan (preview / resolve) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: In p2 show what the guns do under the previewed plan (here: BURST sector 4 into warded Packet 6, 'ward' x2); in p3 show what fired. The data is in state f2; showing it is a HOW decision.
wheel_core.look: Same tracer and result set as the decide state, at plan value (or ghosted) so it is clearly the plan outcome; one tracer style across p1/p2/p3.
wheel_core.problems: p2 draws no tracers at all and p3 draws only bare fire lines (resolve_fire_lines), so the preview hides the only state where a ward bounce happens and the player cannot see their guns change under the plan.

wheel_core.name: Gun muzzle nubs (BURST double shot)
wheel_core.goal: Show the shot leaves this slice, and that BURST fires 2.
wheel_core.look: Two small muzzle pips on the slice rim, drawn as part of the tracer, same cyan, sized to the tracer.
wheel_core.problems: Double circles look like a 'lollipop' or an eye; they overlap the threat trim and the HP ring; size (12 px) bigger than the tracer impact so the start is louder than the end.

wheel_core.name: Brace plate on a slice (p2)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice blocks the next landing entirely this turn'. A player-chosen defence: must read as the player's, not the enemy's.
wheel_core.look: A heavy clamp plate around the wedge with rivets and the Brace glyph disc; colour from the player's side, clearly not the cyan unit shield and not enemy cream.
wheel_core.problems: Cream is the enemy-HP colour (unit HP rows, Adjuster bar), so Brace reads as an enemy element; the glyph disc covers the turret icon; rivets are 10 px dots that read as bolts on a sticker, not a clamp; the plate's corner radius differs from the slice frame under it.

wheel_core.name: Soak chevrons on a slice (p2)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice takes overflow pips instead of your HP' (player-marked END TURN choice). This entry is the inward chevrons; the rim arc, soak break X and soak-lost pip are separate elements of the same token family.
wheel_core.look: Soak token distinct from schedule orange by hue and shape; a toggle the player clearly owns; placed beside the icon, never over it.
wheel_core.problems: Soak #FF9628 is nearly identical to schedule #FF8C1A; inward chevrons mimic enemy hit chevrons, implying damage not absorption; the chevrons sit on top of the SHIELD icon (3.10 rule 4). Four marks for one choice (chevrons, rim arc, break X, soak pip): the family needs pruning to one or two.

wheel_core.name: Soak rim arc on the soaked slice (p2)
wheel_core.goal: Mark the whole slice as soaking, at a glance.
wheel_core.look: If kept: a soak-token edge treatment on the slice frame, not on the threat-trim radius; or removed in favour of the pip and one badge.
wheel_core.problems: soak_marks draws an orange arc, 5.5 px on 9 px ink, at r 142 +/-26 deg: the exact radius and weight of the HARM threat trim, so in p2 it reads as a threat trim in the wrong colour and adds a fourth parallel arc in the band.

wheel_core.name: Soak break X (orange X when soaked to break, p2)
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice breaks at END TURN because you soaked into it' (a chosen break, not an enemy break).
wheel_core.look: The slice_break_x state shape (corner, off the icon) with a soak-token cue, so chosen and forced breaks share one break grammar.
wheel_core.problems: Orange X drawn over the SHIELD icon (3.10 rule 4), in schedule-like orange; same shape as the red break X and the green dead X, so three X marks carry three meanings.

wheel_core.name: Cracked slice mark (white zigzag) - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read 'slice already at 1 pip, holds this turn' without opening the HP bars.
wheel_core.look: A short crack line in the screen glass at the rim, white with ink, consistent with the break X family.
wheel_core.problems: Not drawn in this state (all slices at 2 HP); code draws a 4-point zigzag at 2 px that will vanish at 320 px; must be designed now so the slice state family (intact / cracked / breaks / broken) is one set.

wheel_core.name: Broken slice black-out - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: Read 'this slice is gone, ability lost' (persistent state).
wheel_core.look: Bible 3.22 BROKEN: black-out wedge with red X plus the word or badge; distinct from the breaks-this-turn preview.
wheel_core.problems: Not in this state; code uses a 170-alpha dark wedge and a 7 px red X at the slice centre, the same X as the preview, so preview and final state are indistinguishable.

wheel_core.name: Trigger hit landing on the tower - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: In a Trigger preview, show a pierce that reaches the tower: red pencil to the slice and the hit chevrons on it.
wheel_core.look: Grease pencil in threat red (PENCIL_THREAT) ending in the chevron stack on the slice rim.
wheel_core.problems: Not reached in this state; code uses HARM #FF4433 instead of the bible's PENCIL_THREAT #FF1C2C, so it would look like a unit chevron, not a plan.

wheel_core.name: Spin / Nudge card-hover ghost of the rotated tower - LATENT
wheel_core.goal: On hovering a Spin/Nudge card, show where slices and tracers end up (GDD 9.2 ghost preview on card hover) without losing the live tower.
wheel_core.look: A ghost of the slices and tracers at plan value (outline or 40 percent), clearly secondary to the live wheel; rotation hinted by one plan-pencil arc, never by a media arrow.
wheel_core.problems: Not drawn by the generator; only the Trigger preview exists, so there is no rule for how a rotated-tower ghost reads against the live tower and the threat trim.

wave_rings.name: Empty ring cell (dark glass)
wave_rings.goal: Read 'nothing here' instantly so occupied cells pop; keep the sector grid legible.
wave_rings.look: Bible 3.22: dark glass with a 30 percent lane-style border; uniform fill, faint inner glass highlight.
wave_rings.problems: Empty cells are near-black and larger in area than the units, so the board reads as mostly black holes; each empty cell gets two edges (a dim orange master outline from the board render plus the 30 percent lane border from the overlay); the dashed +2 border reads as grey noise at 320 px.

wave_rings.name: Ring gutters and sector spokes
wave_rings.goal: Separate the three rings (depth) and the six sectors.
wave_rings.look: Even ink gutters, slightly lighter than the backplate, the same width everywhere, continuous with the slice gutters.
wave_rings.problems: Gutter width varies visibly between rings and between occupied and empty cells (unit cells inset 4 px with a 3 deg end inset, empty cells 3 px with 1.5 deg); some spokes are drawn by empty-cell outlines and others by unit cell edges, so the grid is irregular.

wave_rings.name: Unit cell screen (muted mauve wash + programme texture)
wave_rings.goal: Read 'an enemy unit occupies these sectors', its width, and its ring; the cell is the body that chevrons and HP sit on.
wave_rings.look: Darkened, desaturated mauve programme screen (PL10), subtle per-kind tint, value clearly above empty cells and below the red chevrons; flat enough to carry marks.
wave_rings.problems: All kinds share nearly the same mauve; ring-0 and ring-2 cells too close in value so depth reads only from outlines; CRT dot grids moire at 1080p; wide cells show the texture's own corner bezels mid-cell (unit_screen_bezel). Typed hex/code text is a separate element (unit_screen_code_text).

wave_rings.name: Unit screen bezel corners (programme slice frame)
wave_rings.goal: None; it is the slice renderer's family-C frame showing at cell ends.
wave_rings.look: Either a deliberate cell end-cap in the lane colour or removed; one end treatment for every unit.
wave_rings.problems: Pink rounded corners from the programme frame appear at cell ends (e.g. 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock) and inside wide cells, a third outline on top of the lane outline and the HP socket; pink here breaks the 'pink = unit screen fill only' read.

wave_rings.name: Readable hex/code text in unit screens
wave_rings.goal: None; texture only. No legible characters on the board.
wave_rings.look: Same rule as slice_screen_code_text: sub-legible glyph noise under 10 percent contrast or none; never competing with the HP row or chevrons.
wave_rings.problems: Hex columns ('01 00 2C 3F'...) are legible inside the Packet screens (ring 1 sector 0 next to the token, ring 2 sector 5) and survive in p1_nowords; a fourth programme-screen artefact besides moire, the bezel corners and the skull motif.

wave_rings.name: Unit cell lane outline (NOW red / +1 blue / +2 dashed white)
wave_rings.goal: Read ring depth on the unit itself (bible 3.22 four cues): now = solid red 4 px, +1 = solid pale blue 3 px, +2 = dashed white 3 px.
wave_rings.look: One clean outline per cell, inset 4 px, with an ink line outside, dash rhythm fixed.
wave_rings.problems: Outlines are partly hidden under the cream HP sockets and the armor cap; dashed white on ring 2 runs right beside cream HP segments and the white dashed landing lane, three white dashes in a row; ring-0 red outline merges with red chevrons and threat trim.

wave_rings.name: Unit token disc (fill and size)
wave_rings.goal: Anchor each unit: kind (glyph) on a disc that is the hover handle. This entry is the disc fill and size; the lane-style base ring and the dark halo are separate elements.
wave_rings.look: 54 px disc (bible), darkened kind fill one value step off the cell mauve, glyph centred.
wave_rings.problems: 48 px, below the bible's 54; fill nearly the cell's mauve so it reads only by outline; one unit looks different on the board and on its arc disc (arc_glyph_disc is darker).

wave_rings.name: Token lane-style base ring (solid red / solid blue / 14-dash white)
wave_rings.goal: Repeat ring depth on the token itself (depth four ways, 3.1).
wave_rings.look: Fine-tier ring in the lane colour with ink, dash rhythm that survives at 320 px (fewer, longer dashes for +2), same weights as the lane outline tiers.
wave_rings.problems: The 14-dash ring-2 base fills in to a grey ring at 320 px; ring-0 red base merges with the red chevrons beside it; base weights do not follow the lane outline ladder (4/3/3).

wave_rings.name: Token dark halo (ink pool)
wave_rings.goal: Lift the token off busy screens (shadow, 3.7: up to 75 percent, blur 4).
wave_rings.look: Tight soft ink pool, even on all tokens, under 75 percent, never wider than ~6 px past the disc.
wave_rings.problems: Wide dark halo makes a muddy blot on the mauve screen, larger on some tokens than others; it darkens neighbouring HP cream and chevrons.

wave_rings.name: Packet glyph (square with arrow)
wave_rings.goal: Identify the Packet kind (bible 3.22 twin-checked glyphs).
wave_rings.look: White silhouette, ink keyline, the same visual weight as the Worm and Payload glyphs.
wave_rings.problems: The white rounded square is the heaviest glyph on the board and reads as a 'next / skip' media button; arrow points right regardless of travel direction (units travel inward and clockwise), so it implies wrong motion.

wave_rings.name: Worm glyph (zigzag, the 'M' badge)
wave_rings.goal: Identify the Worm kind.
wave_rings.look: Zigzag silhouette that reads as a worm/virus, not a letter.
wave_rings.problems: Reads as the letter M (players will call it 'the M unit'); the glyph is larger than its disc and touches the rim; letter-like glyphs clash with the no-digits/word discipline of the board.

wave_rings.name: Payload glyph (diamond with two bars)
wave_rings.goal: Identify the Payload kind (armored).
wave_rings.look: Diamond with two bars, white with keyline; must not share the diamond shape language used for HP-through and the boss.
wave_rings.problems: Diamond shape collides with red HP-through diamonds and the gold Adjuster diamond (three meanings, one shape); the two bars read as an equals sign.

wave_rings.name: Unit HP row (cream segments in socket)
